notes: AAP curves cover gestation 35 weeks or more; units mg/dL. NICE covers all gestations; units micromol/litre. Never convert when storing; the engine converts.
AAP Supplemental Table 1 gives separate curves for 35, 36, 37, 38, 39 and 40+ weeks without risk factors. Tables 2 to 4 group 38 weeks or more together.

NICE gestation-specific curves below 38 weeks are published only as graphs plus an interactive Excel tool (https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg98/resources/treatment-threshold-graphs-excel-544300525). The construction rule (formula plus straight line from birth) is stored under nice.preterm; the engine draws the curve from it. The Excel data sheet was decoded and matches that rule; it is not stored as a snapshot because its values are formulas, not text.

risk_factors.quote: Hyperbilirubinemia neurotoxicity risk factors include gestational age <38 weeks; albumin <3.0 g/dL; isoimmune hemolytic disease, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) de ﬁciency, or other hemolytic conditions; sepsis; or any signiﬁcant clinical instability in the previous 24 hours.

items.label: Isoimmune hemolytic disease, G6PD deficiency or other hemolytic condition
Significant clinical instability in the previous 24 hours

rules.text: Intensive phototherapy at the hour-specific threshold for gestation and risk factors (Supplemental Table 1 without risk factors, Table 2 with).
rules.quote: Intensive phototherapy is recommended at the total serum bilirubin thresholds in Fig 2 (Supplemental Table 1 and Supplemental Fig 1) or Fig 3 (Supplemental Table 2 and Supplemental Figure 2) on the basis of gestational age, hyperbilirubinemia neurotoxicity risk factors, and age of the infant in hours.

rules.text: Escalation-of-care threshold = exchange transfusion threshold minus 2 mg/dL.
rules.quote: Care should be escalated when an infant ’s TSB reaches or exceeds the escalation-of-care threshold, de ﬁned as 2 mg/dL below the exchange transfusion threshold

rules.text: Urgent exchange transfusion at or above the exchange threshold.
rules.quote: An urgent exchange transfusion should be performed for infants if the TSB is at or above the exchange transfusion threshold.

rules.text: Stopping phototherapy is an option once TSB is at least 2 mg/dL below the threshold at which it was started.
rules.quote: Discontinuing phototherapy is an option when the TSB has decreased by at least 2 mg/dL below the hour-speci ﬁc threshold at the initiation of phototherapy.

rules.text: Measure TSB if TcB is at or within 3 mg/dL of the phototherapy threshold, or TcB 15 mg/dL or more.
rules.quote: TSB should be measured if the TcB exceeds or is within 3 mg/dL of the phototherapy treatment threshold or if the TcB is $15 mg/dL.

rules.text: Use total serum bilirubin; do not subtract direct bilirubin.
rules.quote: Use the total serum bilirubin concentration. Do not subtract direct-reacting or conjugated bilirubin from the total serum bilirubin.

term.quote: Consensus‑based bilirubin thresholds for management of babies 38 weeks or more gestational age with hyperbilirubinaemia
term.comparison: greater than (source prints >value); the 96 row applies from 96 hours onward (source label 96+)

actions.quote: Action | Start phototherapy | Perform an exchange transfusion unless the bilirubin level falls below threshold while the treatment is being prepared

preterm.quote: with a separate graph for each gestational age (from 23 weeks to 37 weeks of gestation)

phototherapy.quote: bilirubin in micromol/litre = (gestational age × 10) − 100 This formula has been proposed for use in paediatric textbooks for many years. Based on informal consensus, the GDG agreed that this formula should be used for babies aged 72 hours or older.

before.shape: straight line from the birth value to the formula value at 72 hours
before.quote: The threshold levels during the first 72 hours were determined by drawing a straight line from a level of 40 micromol/litre (the upper limit of normal for the umbilical cord blood bilirubin) at birth to the formula -based level at 72 hours.

exchange.quote: For preterm babies, the GDG again agreed to us e a simple formula (bilirubin in micromol/litre = gestational age × 10) that has been proposed for use in paediatric textbooks for many years. Based on informal consensus , the GDG agreed that this formula should also be used for babies aged 72 hours or older.

before.shape: straight line from the birth value to the formula value at 72 hours
before.quote: The threshold levels during the first 72 hours were determined by drawing a straight line from a level of 80 micromol/litre at birth to the formula-based level at 72 hours.

rules.text: Stop phototherapy once serum bilirubin is at least 50 micromol/L below the phototherapy threshold.
rules.quote: Stop phototherapy once serum bilirubin has fallen to a level at least 50 micromol/litre below the phototherapy threshold

rules.text: Repeat serum bilirubin 12 to 18 hours after stopping phototherapy.
rules.quote: Check for rebound of significant hyperbilirubinaemia with a repeat serum bilirubin measurement 12–18 hours after stopping phototherapy.

rules.text: Consider intensified phototherapy if bilirubin rises more than 8.5 micromol/L per hour, is within 50 micromol/L below the exchange threshold after 72 hours (see intensify_noresponse for no response).
rules.quote: the serum bilirubin level is rising rapidly (more than 8.5 micromol/litre per hour) the serum bilirubin is at a level within 50 micromol/litre below the threshold for which exchange transfusion is indicated after 72 hours or more since birth
the bilirubin level fails to respond to initial phototherapy (that is, the level of serum bilirubin continues to rise, or does not fall, within 6 hours of starting phototherapy).
If the serum bilirubin level falls during intensified phototherapy to a level 50 micromol/litre below the threshold for which exchange transfusion is indicated reduce the intensity of phototherapy.

rules.text: Well baby, 38 weeks or more, over 24 hours old, bilirubin below but within 50 micromol/L of the phototherapy threshold: repeat within 18 hours with risk factors, within 24 hours without.
rules.quote: In babies who are clinically well, have a gestational age of 38 weeks or more and are more than 24 hours old, and who have a bilirubin level that is below the phototherapy threshold but within 50 micromol/litre of the threshold

repeat.quote: within 18 hours for babies with risk factors for neonatal jaundice
within 24 hours for babies without risk factors.

rules.quote: Do not subtract conjugated bilirubin from total serum bilirubin when making decisions about the management of hyperbilirubinaemia

Note that there is variability between assays from different manufacturers in reported bilirubin measurement. Healthcare professionals should consult their local pathology laboratory when interpreting threshold tables.
